title: Nature does not fundamentally follow continuous differential equations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Nature does not fundamentally follow continuous differential equations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although almost all traditional models in physics (Maxwell, Einstein, Schrödinger equations) are partial differential equations, nature does not fundamentally follow these continuous mathematical abstractions.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is certainly not that nature fundamentally follows these abstractions.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Partial Differential Equations” (from p. 161), p. 162. Scope: fundamental laws of physics

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-23: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.31

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Extensive physical observations exist, but the statement supplies no measurable signature that separates fundamental ontology from highly accurate effective description. Tests become possible only after replacing it with a specific rival model, which changes the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: One could compare predictions of specified continuous and discrete fundamental theories against existing high-energy, gravitational, and precision measurements. Agreement or disagreement would assess those theories, but no finite observation directly decides whether nature fundamentally follows a mathematical abstraction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim names no alternative theory with contrasting predictions.

Continuous and discrete models can be empirically equivalent over accessible scales.

Fundamentally follows is metaphysical without a distinct observable consequence.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.2
data adequacy: 0.12
analysis feasibility: 0.2
data existence: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.18

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: High-precision tests of the classical field equations exist and support those equations as working models. The claim is the further negative statement that nature does not fundamentally follow them. No outcome of those tests distinguishes a fundamental continuum law from an arbitrarily accurate approximation, because the claim names no observable consequence that the two readings do not share.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim says nature does not fundamentally follow partial differential equations such as Maxwell's, Einstein's, and Schrödinger's. Agreement of those equations with experiment is compatible both with their being fundamental and with their being approximations, and the claim states no discrepancy that would decide.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Fundamentally' is not tied to a scale, an observable, or a rival equation with a different prediction.

Any finite-precision success of a continuum equation is compatible with a discrete substrate below the tested scale.
